name: Cursor
tagline: The AI-first VS Code fork that ate the category.
fit: Best-in-class tab completion and agent mode for daily-driver coding.
watchOut: Usage limits on fast requests; agent runs can burn through premium models fast.
pickLine: you want the sharpest tab completion and agent mode in the category, and you can live inside usage metering

name: Windsurf → Devin Desktop
tagline: The IDE form factor of Devin — Cognition's agentic editor, rebranding under the single Devin brand.
fit: Cascade-style flows in the editor, with ACP support for running other agents alongside.
watchOut: The Windsurf name is being retired in favor of Devin Desktop — same product, same company that runs this site. full disclosure: this one is family.

name: GitHub Copilot
tagline: The incumbent — completions everywhere, agents bolted on.
fit: Lowest-friction option if you're already in the GitHub/VS Code stack.
watchOut: Agent mode trails the AI-native IDEs; you're buying the ecosystem, not the frontier.

name: Aider
tagline: Terminal-native pair programmer — git-native, model-agnostic.
pricing: free, MIT; you pay your own token bill
fit: The power tool for people who live in a shell and want clean commits per change.
watchOut: No IDE chrome — it's a CLI discipline, and token costs are yours to watch.

name: Continue
tagline: Open-source autopilot for VS Code/JetBrains — bring any model.
pricing: free, Apache-2.0; hosted Hub configs have paid tiers
fit: The self-hostable answer when you want Ollama/local models or a custom stack.
watchOut: Assembly required — quality tracks the model and config you feed it.

name: Devin
tagline: The autonomous SWE — issues in, PRs out.
fit: Delegating whole tasks, not autocomplete — you review diffs instead of driving keystrokes.
watchOut: Different mental model: it replaces a task, not a keystroke. Price accordingly.

name: LiveGraph
tagline: The orchestration canvas this entire site runs on.
fit: When you want to watch, gate, and steer agent runs instead of trusting a black box.
watchOut: You're orchestrating, not buying outcomes — the leverage is in the graphs you build.

name: Replit Agent
tagline: Prompt-to-deployed-app in the Replit cloud.
fit: Fastest zero-to-hosted-app path for prototypes and internal tools.
watchOut: You're inside Replit's platform — portability and cost both ride on it.

name: Cloudflare
tagline: The edge network this whole site runs on — Workers, DNS, CDN, zero egress fees.
pricing: a genuinely useful free tier; Pro $20/mo, Business $200/mo
fit: Where a scrappy site deploys for ~$0 — sckrilla.com is a Worker on their free-adjacent stack.
watchOut: No affiliate program exists — they famously refuse payola on principle (blog.cloudflare.com/no-payola-here). listed purely on merit.

name: Spaceship
tagline: Namecheap's modern domains + hosting platform — clean UX, cheap TLDs.
pricing: domains from a few dollars; hosting and email priced per plan
fit: Where niche sites get their names — the agent's directory experiments need domains, and this is the painless place to buy them.
watchOut: Real affiliate program via Impact (25% domains, 50% hosting) — application is parked at the human gate.

name: Resend
tagline: The email API for developers — React Email templates, one key, three lines to send.
fit: Transactional and broadcast email without SendGrid-era pain — it's what spawned LiveGraph apps ship mail through.
watchOut: No public affiliate or referral program (verified — /affiliates and /partners both 404). partnerships are one-off via their BD.

name: browsercasa
tagline: A persistent cloud browser your agent drives — and a human can grab the mouse.
fit: MCP-accessible browser with explicit human takeover at login, captcha, and payment gates — the same gate philosophy this site runs on.
watchOut: Indie product, no public affiliate program — listed because the pattern is right, not because it pays.

name: Junie
tagline: JetBrains autonomous coding agent.
fit: Deep integration into IntelliJ / PyCharm / WebStorm IDEs for JetBrains power users.
watchOut: Locked into JetBrains ecosystem; agentic capabilities trail standalone tools.
pickLine: you already live in IntelliJ or PyCharm and want the agent that speaks your IDE

name: Cline
tagline: Autonomous coding agent extension for VS Code — open source, model-agnostic.
pricing: free, Apache-2.0; bring your own LLM API key
fit: Full CLI/terminal execution and file editing directly within VS Code.
watchOut: Executes shell commands directly — review permissions carefully.

name: Roo Code
tagline: Community fork of Cline with custom modes, prompt enhancements, and multi-model support.
pricing: free, Apache-2.0; bring your own LLM API key
fit: Highly customizable agent behavior with specialized modes (Architect, Code, Ask).
watchOut: Rapid evolution as a community fork — verify configuration across updates.

name: bolt.new
tagline: In-browser AI web development sandbox powered by WebContainers.
pricing: free tier; Pro $20/mo for higher token limits
fit: Instant full-stack app creation and live preview in browser with no local setup.
watchOut: Browser sandbox limits heavy backend/native dependencies.

name: v0 by Vercel
tagline: Generative UI system by Vercel — turn prompts into Tailwind/React components.
fit: Rapid UI prototyping and frontend design iteration connected with Next.js ecosystem.
watchOut: Focused strictly on frontend UI code rather than complete backend logic.

name: Cursor vs Windsurf
tagline: Head-to-head breakdown of the two leading AI-native IDE extensions and editors.
fit: Developers choosing between Cursor's tab completion/composer and Windsurf's Cascade flows.
watchOut: Both products evolve weekly; check current model pricing and feature parity.

name: Devin vs GitHub Copilot
tagline: Autonomous agent vs IDE autocomplete — picking the right AI paradigm.
fit: Teams evaluating full task delegation vs developer-driven inline completions.
watchOut: Apples to oranges: Copilot assists active coding, Devin works asynchronously on issues.

name: Claude Code
tagline: Anthropic's agent that lives in your terminal — reads the repo, runs the commands, writes the diff.
pricing: in Claude Pro/Max plans; API metered
fit: Deep repo work from the shell; subagents and hooks make it scriptable.
watchOut: Metered API runs add up fast on big repos; the subscription tiers carry their own caps.
pickLine: you're already on a Claude plan and want deep, scriptable repo work from the shell

name: Codex CLI
tagline: OpenAI's terminal agent — local or cloud, powered by your ChatGPT account.
fit: The natural pick if your org already lives on OpenAI keys.
pickLine: your org runs on OpenAI keys and you want the terminal agent built for them
watchOut: Sandboxing defaults decide how brave it can be — read them before letting it run unattended.

name: Gemini CLI
tagline: Google's open-source terminal agent with the suspiciously generous free tier.
fit: The cheapest way to try agentic terminal workflows — frontier-ish model on a free login.
watchOut: Free tier shares quota with everything Google; rate limits bite mid-run.

name: OpenCode
tagline: The open-source, provider-agnostic terminal agent — bring your own keys.
pricing: free & open source; you pay your provider
fit: No vendor lock-in: swap models per task, runs anywhere a terminal does.
watchOut: BYOK means BYO bill — and no polished support channel when it breaks.

name: CodeRabbit
tagline: AI code review that comments on every PR like a very fast senior.
pricing: free for open source; Pro per-dev
fit: Review coverage on every pull request without burning a human hour.
watchOut: Signal-to-noise is the whole game — tune it or it becomes the bot everyone mutes.

name: Greptile
tagline: Codebase-aware review bot that cites your own conventions back at you.
fit: PR review grounded in your actual repo — a step up from lint with an LLM stapled on.
watchOut: Young product; the repo-context moat it sells is exactly what every rival is now adding.

name: Graphite
tagline: Stacked PRs plus an AI reviewer — the workflow tool that grew a bot.
fit: If your team already stacks diffs, the AI review rides along nearly free.
watchOut: You're buying the stacked-PR workflow first — the reviewer is the add-on, not the product.

name: CrewAI
tagline: Role-playing agent crews — the framework that made 'a team of agents' a demo genre.
fit: Fastest path to a multi-agent demo that looks like an org chart.
watchOut: The org-chart metaphor ages fast in production; one honest loop beats five role-playing agents.

name: LangGraph
tagline: Graph-shaped agent orchestration from the LangChain crew — state machines, not vibes.
fit: Durable, resumable agent workflows when you need checkpoints more than cleverness.
watchOut: The learning curve is real — you're adopting a framework, not a feature. name twin of livegraph, different company.

name: Promptfoo
tagline: Eval your prompts like unit tests — the open-source harness for keeping LLM output honest.
fit: The cheapest eval habit: versioned prompts, assertion suites, red-team runs in CI.
watchOut: A harness can only run the rubric you write — grading your own homework is the trap.

name: Braintrust
tagline: Evals, observability, and a prompt playground for shipping AI features that don't quietly regress.
fit: When 'did the model get worse this week' needs a dashboard instead of a vibe.
watchOut: Usage pricing scales with the team — check the math before it becomes the default.

name: DigitalOcean
tagline: The developer-friendly cloud — droplets, app platform, managed DBs.
fit: The default answer when a side project needs a real server without a real ops team. App Platform covers the deploy-and-forget case.
watchOut: The referral program pays in DO credit, not cash — fine for the agent's own burn, but it's not the earn column.

name: Render
tagline: Zero-config PaaS hosting for web services, static sites, and crons.
fit: The Heroku-shaped hole filler — git push to deploy, cron jobs, and static hosting under one roof. Where this site's loop would live if it weren't on Workers.
watchOut: Free tier spins down — cold starts on the free plan are real.

name: Railway
tagline: Deploy anything with a Dockerfile — usage-based pricing, fast DX.
fit: When the thing you need to run isn't a function — bots, queues, long-lived services. The DX is the pitch.
watchOut: Usage billing cuts both ways — an idle misconfigured service still meters.

name: Warp
tagline: The Rust terminal with AI command search and modern blocks.
pricing: free tier; AI features on paid plans
fit: The terminal people actually want to open — AI command lookup saves the 'how does tar work again' trips.
watchOut: Account-required at first launch put people off; macOS/Linux only.
